events.event: BEI will stop counting High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks in the IHSG calculation from Monday 2 November 2026, and will move periodic index reviews to January/April/July/October.
events.key_numbers: Effective 2 Nov 2026 · periodic reviews moved from Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec to Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct · results effective first trading day of Feb/May/Aug/Nov · incidental evaluations: stocks entering or leaving HSC adjusted immediately · one outlet reports 82 HSC stocks (unverified)
events.why_it_matters: From next Monday the IHSG number people see is calculated differently, which can move the headline index and fund holdings that track it.
events.spreading_evidence: Covered by Media Indonesia, Tirto, Bisnis, Kontan, Metro TV, Kumparan

events.event: The US Fed holds its FOMC meeting on 27-28 October, with markets pricing a smaller chance of an October hike and a near-certain December hike.
events.key_numbers: Fed funds range 3.75-4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September (12-0) · October hike odds ~32% (CME FedWatch), down from ~54% · December hike odds ~90% · decision 28 Oct (6:00 PM per tradingeconomics calendar, time zone not stated)
events.why_it_matters: A Fed hike pulls money out of emerging markets, adding pressure to a rupiah already above Rp18,000 per USD.
events.spreading_evidence: Kompas Money 23 Oct on Fed and rupiah

events.event: Week-ahead global data and central-bank calendar: US Q3 advance GDP and September PCE on 29 Oct, ECB decision on 29 Oct, Bank of Japan decision on 30 Oct.
events.key_numbers: US Q3 GDP consensus ~3.0% (prev 2.2%) · US PCE Sept forecast 0.5% m/m, 3.6% y/y · ECB deposit rate expected 2.5% (hold; hike possible in December) · BoJ policy rate expected 1.25% (hold) · times per tradingeconomics, time zone not stated
events.why_it_matters: Inflation and rate signals from the US, Europe and Japan decide whether foreign money keeps leaving Indonesian stocks and bonds.

events.event: BPS is expected to release October 2026 inflation on or around 2 November, after September inflation hit 3.28% y/y, the highest this year.
events.key_numbers: Sept 2026 inflation 3.28% y/y · 2.17% ytd · 0.30% m/m · CPI 112.31 (108.74 a year earlier) · September data released 1 Oct, 13:59 WIB · October release date not confirmed
events.why_it_matters: Prices of chilli, rice and fuel decide how far a household's money stretches, and BI is already warning on food inflation above 5%.

events.event: Brent crude closed Friday 23 October at its highest in over five months as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and reports of US-Israeli plans against Iran lifted prices.
events.key_numbers: Brent US$117.38 per barrel (close) · WTI US$103.44, +3.99% · detik reported Brent US$115.18 (+1.8%) earlier in the session · ICP September 2026 US$112.81, +US$23.38 from August · APBN 2026 assumption US$70 · Pertalite Rp10,000, Pertamax Rp15,950 unchanged since 2 Sep (Jabodetabek)
events.why_it_matters: Oil far above the US$70 budget assumption strains subsidies and the rupiah, even though Pertalite is promised not to rise this year.
events.spreading_evidence: Detik Finance energy headline; many outlets

events.event: Foreign investors net sold Indonesian shares worth Rp1.28 trillion in the week to 23 October even as the IHSG gained 4.9%.
events.key_numbers: IHSG weekly +4.9% · foreign net sell Rp1.28 T for the week · 23 Oct close 5,439.26 (+0.95%) · value Rp13.85 T · 506 up / 192 down · foreign net sell Rp744.4 bn at midday 23 Oct (headline only)
events.why_it_matters: The rebound is led by local money and buybacks, not foreigners, so it is fragile ahead of the HSC change and MSCI decision.

events.event: Bank Mandiri (BMRI) reported Q3 2026 net profit of Rp45.5 trillion, up 20.7% y/y, ahead of the 27 October date earlier listed for its results.
events.key_numbers: Net profit Rp45.5 T, +20.7% y/y · loans (bank-only) Rp1,605.8 T, +16% · DPK Rp1,750.2 T, +17.7% · assets Rp2,404.1 T · NPL 0.98% · ROE 23.6% · CAR 18.4%
events.why_it_matters: Banks are the biggest weight in the IHSG, and strong profit gives the market a reason to hold on during the MSCI scare.
